templates.name: VMware NSX by HTTP
templates.description:
Monitoring of VMware NSX (NSX-T 3.x, NSX 4.x) through the NSX Manager REST API: management cluster, host transport nodes, edge clusters and edge nodes (status, tunnels, CPU, memory), Tier-0/Tier-1 HA, Tier-0 BGP neighbours and NSX alarms.

Create a host for the NSX Manager cluster (no interface needed), link this template and set {$NSX.MANAGER.URL}, {$NSX.USER}, {$NSX.PASSWORD}. A read-only NSX user (role Auditor) is enough.

Generated by vmware/tools/gen_nsx_template.py.

items.name: NSX: Get Cluster Status
items.description: Collects the overall status of the NSX Management Cluster (management, control and per-service groups). Raw JSON for the dependent items.

triggers.name: NSX: Management cluster is unavailable
triggers.description: detailed_cluster_status.overall_status = UNAVAILABLE: the NSX Manager cluster lost quorum or all nodes are down. The data plane keeps forwarding, but no configuration changes or realization are possible.

triggers.name: NSX: Management cluster is not stable
triggers.description: One or more cluster service groups are degraded. Check System > Appliances in NSX.

triggers.name: NSX: No data from NSX Manager API for {$NSX.NODATA.TIMEOUT}
triggers.description: The master item "NSX: Get Cluster Status" returns no data: wrong URL or credentials, TLS/proxy problem, the API is down, or the user is locked out (see the item error under Monitoring > Latest data).

triggers.name: NSX: Management plane cluster is not stable
NSX: Control plane cluster is not stable
NSX: {ITEM.LASTVALUE1} Manager node(s) offline
triggers.description: A three-node NSX Manager cluster survives the loss of one node; losing a second one makes the cluster read-only.

items.name: NSX: Get transport nodes
items.description: List of transport nodes (ESXi hosts and Edges) for discovery.

items.name: NSX: Get edge clusters
items.description: List of edge clusters and their members, for discovery.

items.name: NSX: Get Tier-0 gateways
items.description: List of Tier-0 gateways for discovery.

items.name: NSX: Get Tier-1 gateways
items.description: List of Tier-1 gateways for discovery.

items.name: NSX: Get BGP neighbors (all Tier-0)
items.description: Walks tier-0s -> locale-services -> bgp/neighbors/status and returns one flat JSON list. Script item instead of HTTP agent: neighbours are two discovery levels deep and Zabbix 7.0 has no nested LLD. Per-gateway errors are returned in "errors" and do not stop the others.

triggers.name: NSX: BGP status could not be read for some Tier-0 gateways

items.name: NSX: Get alarms
items.description: Active system alarms of NSX (status filter {$NSX.ALARM.STATUS}, default OPEN).

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Cluster service groups discovery
discovery_rules.description: Service groups of the management cluster from detailed_cluster_status.groups.

trigger_prototypes.name: NSX: Service group [{#GROUP.TYPE}] is not stable

item_prototypes.name: NSX: Service group [{#GROUP.TYPE}]: members not UP

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Host transport nodes discovery
discovery_rules.description: ESXi host transport nodes (node_deployment_info.resource_type = HostNode). Edge nodes are discovered from edge clusters.

item_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: Get status
item_prototypes.description: GET /api/v1/transport-nodes/<id>/status of an ESXi host transport node.

item_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: overall status
item_prototypes.description: Transport node status: UP, DEGRADED, DOWN or UNKNOWN (aggregates manager/controller connectivity, tunnels and pNICs).

trigger_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: status is DOWN
trigger_prototypes.description: The ESXi host transport node is DOWN: workloads on it lose overlay connectivity.

trigger_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: lost connection to NSX Manager
Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: lost connection to the Central Control Plane

item_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: overlay tunnels status
item_prototypes.description: tunnel_status.status of GENEVE tunnels. UNKNOWN is normal for a host without workloads on overlay segments (no tunnels needed).

trigger_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down
trigger_prototypes.description: tunnel_status.status = DOWN: no GENEVE tunnel (TEP to TEP) is up. Check TEP IP pool, MTU (>= 1600, 1700 recommended) and the transport VLAN.

trigger_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: overlay tunnels degraded
trigger_prototypes.description: Some GENEVE tunnels or their BFD sessions are down.

dependencies.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down
Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.tn.pnic.status[{#NODE.ID}])=2 or last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.tn.pnic.status[{#NODE.ID}])=3
trigger_prototypes.name: Host TN [{#NODE.NAME}]: physical uplink(s) degraded or down

item_prototypes.name: Edge cluster [{#EC.NAME}]: Get status
item_prototypes.description: GET /api/v1/edge-clusters/<id>/status.

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge cluster [{#EC.NAME}]: status is DOWN
trigger_prototypes.description: No member of the edge cluster is UP: north-south routing and stateful services of the gateways placed on it are down.

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge cluster [{#EC.NAME}]: status is DEGRADED
trigger_prototypes.description: At least one edge node of the cluster is not UP: no redundancy.

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Edge nodes discovery
discovery_rules.description: Edge nodes: members of every edge cluster (one entry per member, flattened by JavaScript).

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: Get status
item_prototypes.description: GET /api/v1/transport-nodes/<id>/status of an Edge node (includes CPU/memory in node_status).

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: overall status
item_prototypes.description: Transport node status: UP, DEGRADED, DOWN or UNKNOWN (aggregates manager/controller connectivity, tunnels and pNICs).

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: status is DOWN
trigger_prototypes.description: Edge node {#EDGE.NAME} (member {#EDGE.INDEX} of edge cluster {#EC.NAME}) is DOWN. Its SR instances failed over to the peer, if there is one.

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: lost connection to NSX Manager
Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: lost connection to the Central Control Plane

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: overlay tunnels status
item_prototypes.description: tunnel_status.status of GENEVE tunnels. UNKNOWN is normal for a host without workloads on overlay segments (no tunnels needed).

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down
trigger_prototypes.description: tunnel_status.status = DOWN: no GENEVE tunnel (TEP to TEP) is up. Check TEP IP pool, MTU (>= 1600, 1700 recommended) and the transport VLAN.

trigger_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: overlay tunnels degraded
trigger_prototypes.description: Some GENEVE tunnels or their BFD sessions are down.

dependencies.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down
Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: all overlay tunnels are down

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.edge.pnic.status[{#EDGE.ID}])=2 or last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.edge.pnic.status[{#EDGE.ID}])=3
trigger_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: physical uplink(s) degraded or down

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: datapath CPU usage (avg DPDK core)
item_prototypes.description: Average load of the DPDK (fast path) cores as reported by the Edge. DPDK cores poll constantly, so OS tools show 100%; this value is the real packet-processing load.

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: datapath CPU usage (highest DPDK core)
Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: services CPU usage (avg non-DPDK core)
item_prototypes.description: Cores used by control plane and L7 services (routing daemons, load balancer, VPN, DHCP).

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: memory utilization
item_prototypes.description: edge_mem_usage.system_mem_usage; falls back to mem_used / mem_total on versions without it.

item_prototypes.name: Edge [{#EDGE.NAME}]: uptime
item_prototypes.description: Reported in milliseconds.

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Tier-0 gateways discovery
discovery_rules.description: Tier-0 gateways from /policy/api/v1/infra/tier-0s. ACTIVE_ACTIVE gateways skip the failover triggers (override).

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: Get state
item_prototypes.description: Realized state of the gateway; tier0_status.per_node_status has the HA status of every service router (SR).

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: active SR nodes
item_prototypes.description: Sorted transport node IDs whose SR is ACTIVE. Empty for a gateway without SR (DR only).

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.active.nodes[{#T0.ID}],#1)<>last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.active.nodes[{#T0.ID}],#2) and length(last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.active.nodes[{#T0.ID}],#1))>0 and length(last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.active.nodes[{#T0.ID}],#2))>0
trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: HA failover, active SR moved
trigger_prototypes.description: The set of Edge transport nodes running the ACTIVE service router changed. Expected after maintenance; otherwise check the edge that lost the role (BFD, edge health, uplinks). With preemptive failover mode a second failover follows when it recovers.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: SR nodes ACTIVE
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier0_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: more than one ACTIVE SR in ACTIVE_STANDBY mode (split brain)
trigger_prototypes.description: Both edges consider themselves ACTIVE: BFD between the edges is broken.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: SR nodes STANDBY
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier0_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: SR nodes not ACTIVE/STANDBY
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier0_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: {ITEM.LASTVALUE1} SR node(s) DOWN or not in sync
trigger_prototypes.description: An SR reports DOWN, SYNC or UNKNOWN: the edge is down or cannot reach the peer. For ACTIVE_STANDBY the gateway runs without redundancy; for ACTIVE_ACTIVE ECMP capacity is lost.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: SR nodes total
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier0_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.active[{#T0.ID}])=0 and last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t0.ha.total[{#T0.ID}])>0
trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-0 [{#T0.NAME}]: no ACTIVE service router
trigger_prototypes.description: The gateway has service routers but none is ACTIVE: its north-south traffic and stateful services are down.

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Tier-1 gateways discovery
discovery_rules.description: Tier-1 gateways from /policy/api/v1/infra/tier-1s. Tier-1 without services has no SR: its counters stay 0.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: Get state
item_prototypes.description: Realized state of the gateway; tier1_status.per_node_status has the HA status of every service router (SR).

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: active SR nodes
item_prototypes.description: Sorted transport node IDs whose SR is ACTIVE. Empty for a gateway without SR (DR only).

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.active.nodes[{#T1.ID}],#1)<>last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.active.nodes[{#T1.ID}],#2) and length(last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.active.nodes[{#T1.ID}],#1))>0 and length(last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.active.nodes[{#T1.ID}],#2))>0
trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: HA failover, active SR moved
trigger_prototypes.description: The set of Edge transport nodes running the ACTIVE service router changed. Expected after maintenance; otherwise check the edge that lost the role (BFD, edge health, uplinks). With preemptive failover mode a second failover follows when it recovers.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: SR nodes ACTIVE
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier1_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: SR nodes STANDBY
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier1_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: SR nodes not ACTIVE/STANDBY
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier1_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: {ITEM.LASTVALUE1} SR node(s) DOWN or not in sync
trigger_prototypes.description: An SR reports DOWN, SYNC or UNKNOWN: the edge is down or cannot reach the peer. For ACTIVE_STANDBY the gateway runs without redundancy; for ACTIVE_ACTIVE ECMP capacity is lost.

item_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: SR nodes total
item_prototypes.description: Counted over tier1_status.per_node_status[].high_availability_status.

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.active[{#T1.ID}])=0 and last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.t1.ha.total[{#T1.ID}])>0
trigger_prototypes.name: Tier-1 [{#T1.NAME}]: no ACTIVE service router
trigger_prototypes.description: The gateway has service routers but none is ACTIVE: its north-south traffic and stateful services are down.

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Tier-0 BGP neighbors discovery
discovery_rules.description: One entry per Tier-0 / edge / source address / neighbour.

trigger_prototypes.name: BGP [{#T0.NAME}] {#BGP.SOURCE} -> {#BGP.NEIGHBOR} (AS {#BGP.REMOTE.AS}, {#BGP.EDGE}): session is not ESTABLISHED
trigger_prototypes.description: BGP peering of Tier-0 {#T0.NAME} on edge {#BGP.EDGE} is down. "UNKNOWN" means the neighbour is no longer reported at all (edge down or neighbour removed from the configuration).

item_prototypes.name: BGP [{#T0.NAME}] {#BGP.SOURCE} -> {#BGP.NEIGHBOR} (AS {#BGP.REMOTE.AS}, {#BGP.EDGE}): time since established
item_prototypes.description: time_since_established: seconds in NSX 4.x, milliseconds in NSX-T 2.x/3.x (set {$NSX.BGP.UPTIME.MULTIPLIER} to 0.001 there).

trigger_prototypes.expression: last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.bgp.uptime["{#BGP.UID}"])>0 and last(/VMware NSX by HTTP/nsx.bgp.uptime["{#BGP.UID}"])<{$NSX.BGP.FLAP.PERIOD}
trigger_prototypes.name: BGP [{#T0.NAME}] {#BGP.SOURCE} -> {#BGP.NEIGHBOR} (AS {#BGP.REMOTE.AS}, {#BGP.EDGE}): session flapped (re-established)
trigger_prototypes.description: The session is up but was established less than {$NSX.BGP.FLAP.PERIOD} ago.

discovery_rules.name: NSX: Alarms discovery
discovery_rules.description: Open NSX alarms (JSONPath filter on status) -> one item and one trigger per alarm. The trigger severity is set by overrides from the NSX severity: CRITICAL -> High, HIGH -> Average, MEDIUM -> Warning, LOW -> Info.

item_prototypes.name: NSX alarm {#ALARM.FEATURE} / {#ALARM.EVENT} on {#ALARM.NODE}: status
item_prototypes.description: OPEN while the alarm is active; RESOLVED once it disappears from the list of open alarms.

trigger_prototypes.name: NSX alarm [{#ALARM.SEVERITY}]: {#ALARM.FEATURE} / {#ALARM.EVENT} on {#ALARM.NODE}
